-Box.quick: _-Box <corner1> <corner2> <height> | Third input is height, not Z-coordinate

contexts.default: _-Box 0,0,0 10,10,0 5 - Base rectangle corners + height value. Height is perpendicular to construction plane, not Z-axis.
contexts.center: _-Box _Center 5,5,0 10 8 5 - Center point + width/length/height. Must specify all three dimensions separately, no single cube dimension.
contexts.diagonal: _-Box _Diagonal 0,0,0 10,10,10 - Two 3D corners. Box aligns with world axes, not diagonal direction.

-Box.errors: Height as coordinate fails. _Enter for height uses base width. Missing dimensions in center mode.

-Sphere.quick: _-Sphere <center> <radius> | Use _Diameter/_3Point/_4Point/_FitPoints for alternatives | Points must not be coplanar

contexts.default: _-Sphere 0,0,0 5 creates sphere at origin with radius 5. Most direct method for known center and size.
contexts.diameter: _-Sphere _Diameter <pt1> <pt2> defines sphere using two endpoints as diameter. Useful when you know sphere boundary points.
contexts.3point: _-Sphere _3Point requires three non-coplanar points. Creates unique sphere passing through all three points.
contexts.4point: _-Sphere _4Point uses four points on sphere surface. Points must not be coplanar for valid sphere definition.
contexts.fitpoints: _-Sphere _FitPoints _SelPrev _Enter creates best-fit sphere through pre-selected point objects. Select points first.

-Sphere.errors: Fails without parameters. 3Point/4Point fail with coplanar points. FitPoints requires pre-selected point objects.

-Cylinder.quick: _-Cylinder center radius height | Height must be non-zero

contexts.diameter: Use _Diameter to specify by center + diameter point instead of radius
contexts.3point: Use _3Point for base defined by three non-collinear points + height
contexts.vertical: Use _Vertical to constrain cylinder axis to be vertical
contexts.precision: Default mode most efficient for precise radius values

-Cylinder.errors: Zero height fails | Collinear 3points fail | Same center/diameter point fails

-Cone.quick: _-Cone center radius height | Use DirectionConstraint=None for free axis

contexts.default: _-Cone 0,0,0 5 10 creates vertical cone. Height can be value or apex point coordinate.
contexts.vertical: _-Cone _Vertical forces vertical axis regardless of CPlane orientation.
contexts.diameter: _-Cone _Diameter 0,0,0 10,0,0 10 uses diameter endpoint instead of radius value.
contexts.2point: _-Cone _2Point defines axis direction with two points, then specify radius for base.
contexts.3point: _-Cone _3Point 0,0,0 10,0,0 5,10,0 12 creates base from three non-collinear points.
contexts.directionconstraint: _DirectionConstraint=None allows arbitrary axis orientation, overriding CPlane constraints.

-Cone.errors: Height mixing numeric/coordinate fails. 2Point confusion with diameter. Collinear 3Point fails.

contexts.default: _-Torus 0,0,0 10 3 creates horizontal donut. Major radius = center to tube center, minor = tube thickness. Default XY plane orientation.
contexts.2point: _-Torus _2Point <pt1> <pt2> <minor_radius> defines major diameter with two points. Points set diameter, not radius of major circle.
contexts.vertical: Use _Vertical option for vertical orientation instead of default horizontal (XY plane). Useful for standing torus shapes.
contexts.around_curve: _AroundCurve option creates torus following selected curve path instead of simple circular major radius.

-Torus.errors: Minor radius ≥ major radius = invalid torus. Very small minor radius creates thin ring with poor display quality.

contexts.default: Basic two-point line creation. Start/end points define geometry.
contexts.vertical: Creates Z-axis parallel line. End point Z must differ from start, X/Y must match exactly.
contexts.normal: Surface normal line. Requires valid surface at point, may fail on edges/gaps.
contexts.angled: Angle measured from positive X-axis in current construction plane.
contexts.perpendicular: Requires curve selection first (or _SelPrev). Point determines perpendicular location.
contexts.fourpoint: Creates line between midpoints of two implied lines, not connecting input points.
contexts.bisector: Angle bisector between two lines defined by three points. Length extends from vertex.

-Line.errors: Normal fails without surface. Perpendicular needs curve selection. Vertical requires exact X/Y alignment. Short lengths may be invisible.

-Circle.quick: _-Circle <center> <radius> | Use _Diameter, _3Point, _Tangent, _AroundCurve for alternatives | Tangent needs existing objects

contexts.default: Center-radius is fastest for known dimensions. Use world coordinates or object snaps for precision.
contexts.diameter: Useful when you know diameter endpoints rather than center. Creates circle with diameter between points.
contexts.3point: Perfect for fitting circles to existing geometry. Fails if points are collinear - spread them out.
contexts.tangent: Requires two existing objects first. Use _SelPrev for recently created geometry or _SelId for specific objects.
contexts.aroundcurve: Only works with closed curves like rectangles or polygons. Open curves will be rejected.

-Circle.errors: Tangent mode fails without existing geometry. 3Point fails with collinear points. AroundCurve rejects open curves. _SelPrev fails if no previous object exists.

contexts.default: _-Rectangle <corner1> <corner2> - Two opposite corners define rectangle
contexts.3point: _-Rectangle _3Point <p1> <p2> <p3> - Three points define orientation and shape
contexts.mixed_input: Accepts '10 5' for width/height or full coordinates depending on view

-Rectangle.errors: 3Point mode fails if points don't form valid rectangle geometry

-Polyline.quick: _-Polyline {point1} {point2} ... _Enter | Must Enter to finish, not empty click

contexts.precision: Use exact coordinates (0,0,0 10,0,0) for alignment. Close option connects to start.
contexts.interactive: Click points sequentially. Undo removes last point. Length/Angle constrain next segment.
contexts.modeling: Creates single connected object, not separate lines. Use Explode to break into segments.

-Polyline.errors: Clicking empty space adds unwanted points instead of finishing polyline

-Arc.quick: Creates arcs via 3 points (default), center/radius/angles, or start/direction/end. Avoid collinear points.

contexts.default: Three-point mode: specify start, end, then point on arc. Points must not be collinear or creation fails.
contexts.center: Center mode: specify center point, radius, start angle, end angle. Angles measured from positive X-axis in current CPlane.
contexts.startpoint: Start/direction mode: specify start point, tangent direction vector (unnormalized OK), then endpoint.

-Arc.errors: Fails with collinear points in 3-point mode. Center mode requires valid angle range. Direction vector cannot be zero.

contexts.center: Default mode: center point + two radius points define ellipse axes
contexts.diameter: _Diameter mode: major axis endpoints + minor axis radius
contexts.corner: _Corner mode: ellipse inscribed in rectangle from opposite corners
contexts.fromfoci: _FromFoci mode: two focus points + any point on ellipse perimeter

-Ellipse.errors: _Center needs 3 points not center+radii | _Corner fits within rectangle not through corners

-ExtrudeCrv.quick: _-ExtrudeCrv _Pause [distance] | Solid option only works with closed curves

contexts.default: Extrudes curves as surfaces. Use _Pause for pre-selection, specify direction vector (e.g., 0,0,10) or distance. Open curves create surfaces only.
contexts.solid: Set _Solid=_Yes for closed curves only. Creates 3D solids instead of surfaces. Requires closed planar curves as input for proper solid generation.
contexts.solid=_yes: Direct solid extrusion mode with pre-selected curves. Automatically applies solid option, requires distance parameter and closed curve input.

-ExtrudeCrv.errors: Fails without curve selection. Solid mode fails on open curves. Missing direction/distance causes prompts that break automation.

-Loft.quick: _-Loft curves _Enter | Style/Type control smoothness | Need 2+ curves

contexts.default: _-Loft prompts for curve selection, then creates surface with default normal style
contexts.style_preset: _-Loft _Style=_Tight sets smoothness before selection - _Normal balanced, _Loose flexible, _Tight constrained
contexts.type_runtime: _-Loft _SelPrev _Type=Normal _Enter sets smoothness after selection with pre-selected curves
contexts.with_preselection: Pre-select curves then _-Loft _SelPrev _Enter for streamlined workflow

-Loft.errors: Fails with <2 curves, incompatible curve orientations, or unsuitable curve geometry for surface creation

-PlanarSrf.quick: _-PlanarSrf _Pause | Curves must be closed and coplanar

contexts.default: Select closed planar curves to fill with surface. Use DeleteInput to remove originals, Holes option for nested curves creating voids. All curves must lie in same plane.

-PlanarSrf.errors: Open curves rejected. Non-planar curves fail. Self-intersecting curves give unexpected results.

-Move.quick: _-Move [selection] base_point target_point | Fails silently without selection

contexts.default: Non-interactive move requiring explicit object selection first. Use _SelId or selection commands before calling. Movement vector defined by base to target points.
contexts.scripting: Essential for automated workflows. Chain with selection commands like _SelId. No user prompts make it ideal for batch operations and macros.
contexts.precision: Coordinates in current coordinate system. Use precise numeric values for exact positioning. Base/target points define exact movement vector for predictable results.

-Move.errors: Silent failure without selection. Invalid coordinates cause command abort. Missing base/target points halt execution.

contexts.single_copy: Select objects, Enter, pick base point, pick one target point, Enter to finish
contexts.multiple_copies: After base point, specify multiple target points before final Enter - creates copies at each location
contexts.precise_placement: Use coordinates for exact positioning: base point 0,0,0 then target 10,0,0 for 10-unit X offset

-Copy.errors: Forgetting second Enter leaves command hanging | Wrong base point changes copy positioning unexpectedly

-Rotate.quick: Syntax: _-Rotate [selection] [center_point] [angle] | Must select objects first, angle in degrees

contexts.scripting: Non-interactive rotation ideal for automation. All parameters required upfront: selection, center point (x,y,z), and angle in degrees. No prompts or user interaction.
contexts.precision: Specify exact center point coordinates even for object-centered rotations. Angle follows right-hand rule around Z-axis (positive = counterclockwise from above).
contexts.batch_operations: Efficient for rotating multiple objects with same parameters. Can use object IDs for selection, then specify single center and angle for all selected geometry.

-Rotate.errors: Fails without object selection. Requires explicit center point coordinates. Angle must be numeric (degrees not radians).

contexts.scripting: No prompts - must provide all parameters in order. Use _Pause for pre-selection or specify objects directly.
contexts.automation: Perfect for batch operations. Scale factor 2=double, 0.5=half, negative values mirror+scale.
contexts.precision: Base point critical - objects scale away from this point. Use 0,0,0 for origin-based scaling.

-Scale.errors: Scale factor 0 collapses to point. Missing parameters fail silently. Wrong base point gives unexpected results.

-Mirror.quick: _-Mirror [selection] [point1] [point2] | Must select objects first, then define mirror line with 2 points

contexts.modeling: Mirror geometry across construction lines or centerlines. Use world coordinates or object snaps for precise mirror planes. Common for creating symmetric parts.
contexts.drafting: Mirror 2D elements across axes or reference lines. Useful for architectural plans, mechanical drawings. Mirror plane extends infinitely beyond the two defining points.
contexts.scripting: Requires pre-selection or _SelId. Use _Pause for interactive point picking or exact coordinates. Consider Copy=Yes option to retain originals in automated workflows.

-Mirror.errors: Fails without object selection. Invalid with single point or coincident points. Non-geometric objects may not mirror properly.

-BooleanUnion.quick: -BooleanUnion: Combines solids into one. Requires valid closed solids/surfaces.

contexts.default: Select multiple solid objects, press Enter. Result is single unified solid. Non-overlapping objects become joined parts of one object.

-BooleanUnion.errors: Fails with open surfaces, invalid solids, or tiny gaps between objects. Complex intersections may create invalid results.

-BooleanDifference.quick: Subtracts solids: select objects to subtract FROM, then objects to subtract

contexts.default: Interactive selection in two phases - first select target objects (what you want to keep modified), then select cutting objects (what removes material). Both must be closed solids/surfaces that actually intersect.

-BooleanDifference.errors: Fails if objects aren't closed solids, don't intersect, or selection order is wrong

contexts.modeling: Creates new solid from intersection volume of closed solids. Original objects deleted by default. Use for finding common volumes between parts.
contexts.troubleshooting: Check objects actually intersect with overlapping volume. Ensure all inputs are closed solids, not surfaces. Try SimplifyCrv on complex geometry first.

-BooleanIntersection.errors: Fails if no intersection volume exists, open surfaces selected, or geometry too complex

contexts.curves: Joins curves at endpoints only. Open curves need touching endpoints. Closed curves won't join to each other.
contexts.surfaces: Joins surfaces along shared edges. Surfaces must have coincident or very close boundaries to merge successfully.
contexts.polysurfaces: Combines polysurfaces into single object. All faces must form valid closed volume or connected surface network.
contexts.mixed_objects: Cannot join curves to surfaces or different object types. Use separate operations for different geometry types.

-Join.errors: Fails silently if objects don't touch, wrong types selected, or tolerance too tight

-Explode.quick: -Explode: Breaks complex objects into components. Not all objects explodable.

contexts.polysurfaces: Explodes into individual surfaces - may lose solid properties. Use Join to recombine if needed.
contexts.blocks: Destroys block definition relationship permanently. Use BlockEdit to modify block definition instead.
contexts.groups: Separates grouped objects. Similar to Ungroup but works on more object types.
contexts.hatches: Breaks hatch into boundary curves and fill pattern elements.
contexts.text_dimensions: Creates many small curve segments - often undesirable for editing.

-Explode.errors: Fails silently on unexplodable objects (curves, points, simple surfaces). No error message given.

contexts.curves: Creates parallel curves at specified distance. Use _Pause for interactive distance input or direct numeric value. Watch curve direction for offset side.
contexts.surfaces: Offsets surfaces inward/outward by distance. Complex surfaces may fail. Self-intersecting results possible with large distances.
contexts.scripting: Use _-Offset _Pause [distance] for interactive or _-Offset [numeric_distance] for direct input. Requires pre-selected objects.

-Offset.errors: Complex geometry fails to offset, self-intersections create invalid results, direction opposite to expected

-Intersect.quick: -Intersect: Creates curves at intersection points between two sets of objects. Requires two separate selections.

contexts.default: -Intersect selects first set, then second set. Creates intersection curves with document tolerance.
contexts.tolerance: -Intersect _Tolerance [value] sets custom tolerance before selection. Affects intersection detection sensitivity.
contexts.deleteinput: -Intersect _DeleteInput removes original objects after creating intersection curves. Useful for cleanup.
contexts.keepinput: -Intersect _KeepInput preserves original objects. Default behavior for maintaining source geometry.
contexts.all: -Intersect _All intersects all document objects with selected set. Efficient for comprehensive intersections.
contexts.group: -Intersect _Group creates grouped intersection curves. Helps organize complex intersection results.

-Intersect.errors: No curves created if objects don't intersect in 3D. Wrong tolerance misses intersections or creates false positives.

-IntersectSelf.quick: -IntersectSelf: finds self-intersection points on curves | dash bypasses dialogs

contexts.curve_analysis: Analyzes selected curves for self-intersections, creating point objects at intersection locations. Useful for quality control of complex curves or identifying problematic geometry.
contexts.batch_processing: Command-line version ideal for scripts and batch operations since it bypasses dialog boxes. Ensure proper curve selection before running to avoid unexpected results.
contexts.cleanup_workflow: Often used with SelSelfIntersectingCrv to first identify then analyze problematic curves. Consider point cleanup after analysis to avoid model clutter.

-IntersectSelf.errors: Produces no output on simple curves without self-intersections; creates clutter with many intersection points

-IntersectTwoSets.quick: _-IntersectTwoSets _SelLast _SelPrev | Needs two separate curve selections in history

contexts.default: Uses selection history to define curve sets. Select first group, then second group, then run command. _SelLast gets most recent selection, _SelPrev gets previous one. Only works with curves.

-IntersectTwoSets.errors: Fails if only one selection exists, wrong object types (surfaces/solids), or selection history is unclear

contexts.default: Center point then three radii or axis endpoints. Can mix radii values with coordinate points but syntax differs.
contexts.diameter: Define one axis with two points, then specify remaining two radii as length values.
contexts.3point: Three points define axis directions - ellipsoid orientation determined by point positions.
contexts.2point: Two points define one axis, remaining axes specified as radius lengths perpendicular to first axis.
contexts.vertical: Creates upright ellipsoid - center point, two horizontal radii, then vertical height.
contexts.fitpoints: Select existing points first, then run command. Ellipsoid fits through selected point cloud.

-Ellipsoid.errors: Invalid radius combinations fail silently. FitPoints requires pre-selected points or fails. Coordinate format x,y,z strict - spaces around commas cause failure.

-Plane.quick: Creates planar surfaces. Default: corner-to-corner rectangle. _3Point for arbitrary orientation. _Vertical for upright planes.

contexts.default: Two corner points define rectangular plane aligned to current construction plane. Good for basic floor/wall surfaces.
contexts.3point: Three non-collinear points define plane orientation. Essential for angled surfaces or when construction plane alignment inadequate.
contexts.vertical: Base point + direction + height creates upright plane. Useful for walls, partitions, or vertical reference surfaces.

-Plane.errors: Collinear points in 3Point mode fail. Vertical height of zero creates invisible plane. Check model scale for appropriate dimensions.

contexts.numsides: Standard mode: specify sides count, center point, then radius. Use _Circumscribed/_Inscribed for circle relationship, _Edge for edge length input instead of radius
contexts.scripting: Dash prefix essential for automation. Sequence: NumSides option, number value, center coordinates, radius value. No dialog interruptions
contexts.modeling: Creates in current CPlane. Consider using Circumscribed for polygons around existing circles, Inscribed for polygons within circles

-Polygon.errors: Fails with <3 sides. Wrong parameter sequence breaks command. Missing dash shows dialog in scripts

-Pyramid.quick: -Pyramid <center> <corner> <height> | Base corner sets both size and orientation

contexts.default: Creates square-based pyramid from center point, corner point defining base dimensions, and height value. Base corner determines both size and rotation of the square base.

-Pyramid.errors: Negative height creates downward pyramid; base is always square regardless of corner position

contexts.modeling: Creates hollow cylinders for pipes, sleeves, bushings. Wall thickness defines material depth, not inner dimension.
contexts.architectural: Useful for columns, ducts, structural tubes. Height extends upward from base center point.
contexts.mechanical: Perfect for flanges, spacers, cylindrical housings. Inner radius = outer radius minus thickness.

-Tube.errors: Fails if thickness ≥ radius (no hollow space) or negative values

-RectangularLight.quick: Creates rectangular area light: _-RectangularLight <center> <width> <height> | Must provide complete 3D coordinates

contexts.default: Center point + dimensions mode: specify center point, then width and height values. Both dimensions required.
contexts.target: Directional lighting: _Target option sets light direction first, then center point and dimensions follow.
contexts.three_point: Corner definition mode: specify three corner points to define rectangle shape and orientation in 3D space.

-RectangularLight.errors: Incomplete coordinates fail | Missing width/height fails | Creates render lights, not viewport geometry

-ArcBlend.quick: _-ArcBlend curve1 curve2 _Enter | Fails if curves too far apart or parallel

contexts.automation: Use _SelId for precise curve selection. Check geometry compatibility before execution to avoid failures.
contexts.interactive: Visual feedback shows potential blend. Adjust curve positions if blend preview doesn't appear.
contexts.precision: Radius option controls blend tightness. Trim/Join options affect final geometry structure.

-ArcBlend.errors: Fails: parallel curves, excessive distance, coincident curves. No arc created if geometrically impossible.

-BlendCrv.quick: Creates smooth blend curve between two curves. Syntax: -BlendCrv. May fail if curves too far apart.

contexts.curve_connection: Automatically matches tangency at blend points. Use continuity options for position/tangency/curvature control. Bulge parameter shapes the blend.
contexts.troubleshooting: If blend fails: check curve proximity, try Reverse option for better end matching, verify curves aren't self-intersecting or degenerate.
contexts.workflow_integration: Often used after Trim/Split operations. Consider FilletCurves for corner blending, Connect for simple joining, Loft for multi-curve blending.

-BlendCrv.errors: Fails when curves too distant, poor end orientations, or incompatible geometries. No visual feedback until completion.

-CloseCrv.quick: Closes open curves with straight line between endpoints. Only works on open curves.

contexts.default: Interactive selection of open curves to close. Creates straight line segment connecting endpoints, not smooth connection.

-CloseCrv.errors: Fails silently on closed curves. May create self-intersecting geometry if endpoints are distant or curve loops back.

-Conic.quick: Creates conic sections. Syntax: focus1 focus2 point_on_curve rho_value. Rho: 0-1=ellipse, 1=parabola, >1=hyperbola

contexts.ellipse_creation: Use rho between 0-1. Lower values create more circular ellipses, higher values more elongated. Focus points define major axis direction.
contexts.parabola_creation: Set rho exactly to 1.0. Focus points define parabola orientation. Point on curve determines opening direction and size.
contexts.hyperbola_creation: Use rho > 1. Higher values create more open hyperbolas. Only one branch is created through the specified point.
contexts.precision_work: Focus points cannot be coincident. Point on curve must not be collinear with foci or command fails silently.

-Conic.errors: Fails if focus points coincident or point collinear with foci. Invalid rho values may create unexpected shapes or fail.

contexts.architectural: Perfect for cable structures, suspension elements, chain modeling - natural hanging curve physics
contexts.engineering: Structural cables, power lines, bridge design - mathematically accurate catenary physics
contexts.artistic: Organic flowing curves, fabric draping simulation, natural suspension forms

-Catenary.errors: Negative sag fails; extreme sag creates unusable curves; requires valid point pair

-CrvEnd.quick: _-CrvEnd | Creates point at curve end parameter (may not be visually obvious for closed curves)

contexts.default: Select curve → Enter. Creates point object at curve's end parameter. Only uses first curve if multiple selected. Works only with curve objects, not surfaces.

-CrvEnd.errors: Fails on non-curve geometry. Closed curves: end point location may be unexpected based on parameterization.

-CrvStart.quick: _-CrvStart creates point at curve start parameter | Start depends on parameterization, not visual direction

contexts.point_extraction: Creates actual point object at curve start parameter. Use when you need persistent geometry marking curve beginning for further operations or reference.
contexts.curve_analysis: Reveals curve parameterization direction - start parameter may be opposite to expected visual direction. Useful for understanding curve orientation before operations.
contexts.automation: Requires curve selection via _SelId or interactive picking. Point created inherits current layer/properties. Combine with -CrvEnd for full curve endpoints.

-CrvStart.errors: Fails on surfaces/non-curve geometry | Creates object, doesn't just locate | Start may be visually unexpected end

-CrvSeam.quick: Moves seam point on closed curves. Only works on closed curves, point must lie on curve path.

contexts.default: Select closed curve first, then specify new seam location with coordinates. Point should be on or very close to the curve path for best results.

-CrvSeam.errors: Fails on open curves (no seam exists). Point far from curve may give unexpected results or fail.

-CrvDeviation.quick: -CrvDeviation: Select two curves to measure deviation distance. Requires exactly two valid curve objects.

contexts.quality_control: Essential for verifying curve accuracy after operations like fitting, simplifying, or importing. Compare original vs processed curves to ensure acceptable deviation tolerances.
contexts.surface_analysis: Use before surface creation to ensure input curves meet deviation requirements. Critical for Class-A surfacing where curve continuity affects surface quality.
contexts.import_validation: Verify imported curves against reference geometry. Different CAD systems may introduce slight deviations during translation that need quantification.

-CrvDeviation.errors: Fails with insufficient selections, non-curve objects, or invalid geometry. Complex curves may cause performance issues during detailed analysis.

-ContinueCurve.quick: Extends existing curve from endpoint. Syntax: _-ContinueCurve _SelId {id} _Enter

contexts.default: Interactive mode prompts for curve selection, then continuation parameters. Use _SelId for programmatic selection of specific curve by ID.

-ContinueCurve.errors: Fails without existing curve. Must select endpoint, not middle. Some curve types non-continuable.

-ContinueInterpCrv.quick: Extends interpolated curves by adding points. Syntax: _-ContinueInterpCrv _SelLast _Enter. Only works on InterpCrv objects, extends from end only.

contexts.curve_modeling: Essential for building complex interpolated curves incrementally. Use after InterpCrv to add more control points without starting over. Maintains curve continuity.
contexts.automation: _SelLast automates curve selection for recently created objects. Useful in scripts where you know the target curve is the last created interpolated curve.
contexts.interactive_design: Allows iterative curve building - create initial curve with InterpCrv, then use ContinueInterpCrv to refine and extend based on visual feedback.

-ContinueInterpCrv.errors: Fails if selected object isn't an interpolated curve. _SelLast fails if no recent objects or wrong type. Cannot extend from curve start, only end.

-ApplyCrv.quick: _-ApplyCrv _SelLast _Enter _SelPrev _Enter | Order matters: curve first, then surface

contexts.default: Select curve to apply, then target surface. Uses _SelLast for curve, _SelPrev for surface. Requires both objects to be geometrically compatible for successful application.

-ApplyCrv.errors: Fails if no curve/surface available, wrong selection order, or geometric incompatibility between objects

contexts.default: Select objects first, then curve path. Control copies count, spacing method (equal/distance), and orientation relative to curve direction. Works with any valid curve geometry.

-ArrayCrv.errors: Fails if curve too short for object size, invalid curve selection, or complex curves causing orientation issues

-CreateUVCrv.quick: Creates UV parameter curves on surface | Only works on surfaces, not polysurfaces

contexts.surface_analysis: Visualizes parametric structure of surfaces for understanding UV flow and surface construction quality
contexts.modeling_workflow: Useful for checking surface parameterization before texturing or further operations requiring good UV layout
contexts.troubleshooting: Helps diagnose surface issues by revealing parameter direction problems or irregular UV distribution

-CreateUVCrv.errors: Fails on polysurfaces/meshes | Complex surfaces create viewport clutter | UV directions may not match visual expectations

-Array.quick: Creates multiple copies in rectangular/polar patterns. Must select objects first.

contexts.rectangular: Grid pattern: _-Array _Rectangular [rows] [columns] [levels] [x_spacing] [y_spacing] [z_spacing]. Negative spacing reverses direction.
contexts.polar: Circular pattern: _-Array _Polar [center_point] [number_of_items] [angle_to_fill]. Use 360 for full circle.
contexts.default: Interactive mode prompts for array type then parameters. Good for exploring options.

-Array.errors: Fails without object selection. Zero spacing stacks objects. Large arrays slow performance.

-Helix.quick: _-Helix {center} {radius} {axis_end} {turns} | Use _Vertical for height instead of axis end point

contexts.default: Standard helix: center point, radius, axis end point, turn count. Axis end point defines both direction and height of helix.
contexts.vertical: Vertical helix using height parameter instead of axis end point. More intuitive for straight vertical helixes with known height.
contexts.aroundcurve: Wraps helix around existing curve path. Must select curve first, then helix follows curve's shape and direction.

-Helix.errors: Negative radius causes unexpected results. AroundCurve fails without curve selection. Confusing axis end point vs height parameters.

contexts.default: _-Spiral creates 3D spiral around custom axis vector. Requires center point, radius, axis direction (use unit vectors), turns count, and pitch distance.
contexts.vertical: _-Spiral _Vertical creates vertical spiral with total height parameter instead of axis vector. Good for consistent vertical helixes.
contexts.flat: _-Spiral _Flat creates planar spiral in current CPlane. No axis/height needed - only center, radius, turns, and pitch spacing.

-Spiral.errors: Wrong parameter count for mode fails. Non-unit axis vectors create unpredictable results. Set CPlane before _Flat mode.

-InterpCrv.quick: _-InterpCrv point1 point2 ... | Need 2+ points, degree ≤ points-1

contexts.default: _-InterpCrv 0,0,0 5,5,0 10,0,0 - auto degree based on point count

-InterpCrv.errors: Fails with <2 points or degree > point_count-1

-Parabola.quick: _-Parabola <pt1> <pt2> <pt3> | _Vertex/_Focus modes available | Three points must not be collinear

contexts.default: Creates parabola through three points. Points define start, end, and curve position. Non-collinear points required for unique definition.
contexts.vertex: Define by vertex point, axis direction, and focal parameter. Focal parameter controls parabola width - larger values = wider curves.
contexts.focus: Define by focus point, axis direction, and focal parameter. Focus is the geometric focal point of the parabolic curve.

-Parabola.errors: Collinear points in default mode fail. Invalid focal parameters cause errors. Axis direction cannot be zero vector.

-Pipe.quick: _-Pipe: Creates pipe surface around curves. Requires curve selection first.

contexts.modeling: Use for creating tubular geometry like handrails, conduits, or structural elements. Set appropriate radius for curve tightness to avoid geometry failures.
contexts.parametric: Point option allows variable radius along curve length. Thick option creates hollow pipes with wall thickness for realistic modeling.
contexts.finishing: Cap options (Flat/Round/None) control pipe end treatment. Multiple curves create separate objects - use Join if single pipe needed.

-Pipe.errors: Fails silently without curve selection. Small radius on tight curves causes self-intersection failures.

-Hyperbola.quick: Creates hyperbolic curve. Default: 3 points. _Foci: 2 foci + point on curve. Points can't be collinear.

contexts.default: Uses start point, end point, and control point on curve. Points define hyperbola shape through geometric relationship. Avoid collinear points which prevent construction.
contexts.foci: Mathematical definition using two focus points and point on curve. Point placement determines hyperbola branch and eccentricity. Distance difference to foci must be constant.

-Hyperbola.errors: Collinear points fail construction. Points too close create degenerate shapes. Invalid foci-point relationships produce unexpected curves.

-Sweep1.quick: -Sweep1 [rail_curve] [profile_curve] | Rail first, profile second - no Enter between

contexts.default: -Sweep1 selects rail curve first, then profile curve. Order is critical - rail defines path, profile defines cross-section. Don't press Enter after rail selection, proceed directly to profile.

-Sweep1.errors: Fails with self-intersecting curves or invalid geometry. Selection order matters - rail must come first.

-Sweep2.quick: _-Sweep2 [rail1] [rail2] [profile] | Rails must not intersect except at endpoints

contexts.roadlike: Use Roadlike=Yes to keep cross-section perpendicular to rails, essential for architectural sweeps like handrails or moldings
contexts.complex_geometry: For twisted rails, ensure similar parameterization and position profile near rail start. Use SimpleSweep=Yes if standard algorithm fails
contexts.closed_surfaces: Set Closed=Yes for continuous loops. Profile curve position relative to rail endpoints affects surface orientation

-Sweep2.errors: Fails when rails intersect mid-span, profile too far from rails, or incompatible rail curvature

-Curve.quick: _-Curve {pt1} {pt2} {pt3}... | Control points don't lie ON curve except endpoints

contexts.default: Creates NURBS curve with automatic degree based on point count. Enter points sequentially, press Enter to finish. Curve passes through endpoints only.
contexts.degree=5: Explicit degree setting requires minimum 6 points (degree+1). Higher degrees create smoother curves with broader control point influence zones.
contexts.coordinate_input: Accepts 3D coordinates as x,y,z or 2D as x,y (z=0). Mix coordinate formats within same command for varied elevation control.

-Curve.errors: Insufficient points for degree fails silently. High degree with few points creates unexpected shapes. Missing coordinate separators.

-Revolve.quick: Revolves objects around axis. Syntax: _-Revolve [selection] start_point end_point. Closed curves→solids, open→surfaces.

contexts.default: Prompts for start/end angles. Objects must not intersect axis unless intentional. Axis direction affects result orientation.
contexts.fullcircle: Use _FullCircle option for 360° revolution. Skips angle prompts. Most common for creating complete rotational forms.

-Revolve.errors: Fails if axis points identical or objects unsuitable for revolution. Self-intersecting results from poor object positioning.

-NetworkSrf.quick: -NetworkSrf: Creates surface from intersecting curve network | Curves must intersect properly

contexts.default: Interactive mode prompts for curve selection. Use for visual feedback when building complex surface networks.
contexts.command_line: Non-interactive scripting mode. Combine with selection commands like _SelAll for automated workflows.
contexts.EdgeContinuity: Controls how surface meets edge curves - Position for basic fit, Tangency/Curvature for smooth blending.
contexts.InteriorContinuity: Sets smoothness at curve intersections - critical for avoiding surface kinks at network nodes.
contexts.Tolerance: Balance between accuracy and surface complexity - tight tolerance may fail, loose creates poor fit.
contexts.TrimAndSplit: Automatically processes surface at intersections - useful for creating multiple surface patches.

-NetworkSrf.errors: Fails with isolated curves or improper networks. Complex intersections cause surface generation failure.

-Patch.quick: -Patch: Creates patch surface from curves/points via command-line. Requires selection first.

contexts.modeling: Use for filling gaps between curve networks. Better control than NetworkSrf for simple patches. Consider curve continuity for smooth results.
contexts.repair: Excellent for patching holes in surfaces. Select boundary curves carefully - gaps or overlaps cause failures. Preview before accepting.
contexts.automation: Command-line mode bypasses dialog for scripting. Parameters must be input sequentially through prompts. Test interactively first.

-Patch.errors: Fails without curves/points selected. Poor curve arrangement creates twisted patches. Discontinuous curves produce rough surfaces.

-FilletEdge.quick: _-FilletEdge _NextRadius [value] [selection] | Radius must be < smallest face dimension

contexts.default: _-FilletEdge [selection] uses current radius. Select edges individually for precise control over which edges get filleted.
contexts.nextradius: _-FilletEdge _NextRadius [value] sets new radius first. Use _AllEdges for all edges or select specific edges for partial filleting.
contexts.batch: _AllEdges applies to entire object - may create unexpected results on complex geometry. Test with smaller radius first.
contexts.troubleshooting: If filleting fails, try smaller radius values. Complex intersections and thin walls are common failure points.

-FilletEdge.errors: Radius too large for geometry, complex intersections fail, _AllEdges on intricate objects creates topology issues

-Point.quick: _-Point x,y,z | Use _Multiple for sequence | Enter/Esc to exit multiple mode

contexts.default: Creates single point at coordinate. Format: _-Point 0,0,0. Point becomes selectable object in model.
contexts.multiple: Continuous point placement with _-Point _Multiple. Each click/coordinate creates point. Must manually exit with Enter/Esc.

-Point.errors: Missing commas in coordinates fails. Points invisible at small zoom. Forgetting exit in multiple mode continues command.

-Points.quick: _-Points x,y,z x,y,z ... | No spaces in coordinates | Dash required

contexts.coordinate_list: Provide space-separated coordinate triplets like 0,0,0 5,5,0 10,0,0. Each triplet must be comma-separated with no internal spaces. Command executes immediately without prompts.

-Points.errors: Fails on spaces within coordinates (0, 0, 0), missing dash prefix, or malformed triplets

-Text.quick: _-Text "text content" x,y,z | Quote spaces, dash bypasses dialogs

contexts.scripting: Use quotes for multi-word text. Coordinates required as x,y,z format. May prompt for height/font if not preset in document.
contexts.automation: Dash version skips some UI dialogs. Text height inherits from current settings or prompts. Position must be explicit coordinates.
contexts.batch_creation: Consistent syntax with quoted strings. Each text object needs separate command call. Font settings apply to all until changed.

-Text.errors: Unquoted spaces split text into parameters. Missing coordinates cause position prompts. Invalid coordinate format fails silently.

-TextObject.quick: _-TextObject _Height=5 Hello 0,0,0 | Height before text, no spaces in coords

contexts.height_specified: Pre-set height with _Height={value}, then text content, then x,y,z coordinates. Minimal dialogue when height specified upfront.
contexts.scripting: Use underscores for non-interactive mode. Text with spaces may need quotes or special handling in automated workflows.
contexts.coordinate_placement: Coordinates as comma-separated x,y,z without spaces. Text placed at exact 3D location with specified height in current units.

-TextObject.errors: Height must precede text content or command fails. Spaces in coordinates cause parsing errors. Text with spaces may break command parsing.

-PointCloud.quick: _-PointCloud x1,y1,z1 x2,y2,z2 | Exact comma format, press Enter to complete

contexts.coordinate_input: Input multiple points as x,y,z coordinates separated by spaces. Each coordinate must use exact comma format with no spaces within. Press Enter when done adding points.
contexts.default: Creates point cloud from specified coordinates. Minimum input needed but more points create better cloud representation. Command completes when input sequence finished.

-PointCloud.errors: Fails with incorrect coordinate format (spaces in x,y,z). May not create object if insufficient points or input not properly terminated.

contexts.modeling: Sets working plane for drawing/construction operations. Use 3 points for precise orientation when 2-point plane isn't aligned as expected.
contexts.drafting: Establishes construction plane for 2D drafting operations in 3D space. Plane becomes active CPlane for subsequent commands.
contexts.scripting: Automates CPlane setup for batch operations. Consider using SetCPlane afterward to make plane current for following commands.

-PlaneThroughPt.errors: Fails with collinear points (need 3rd non-collinear). Creates infinite construction plane, not surface object.

-DupBorder.quick: -DupBorder | Duplicates borders of selected objects | Must select objects with actual borders first

contexts.default: -DupBorder after selecting objects with borders. Combine with _SelLast for recent selections. Check layer organization as duplicated borders appear on top of originals.

-DupBorder.errors: Fails on objects without borders or incompatible geometry types. No selection = no action.

-ArrayPolar.quick: -ArrayPolar center_point count angle | Count includes original object

contexts.command_line: Bypasses dialog for scripting. Syntax: -ArrayPolar [center] [count] [angle]. Essential for automation workflows.
contexts.default: Interactive mode with dialog. Use _SelLast to array last selected objects. Good for manual design work with visual feedback.

-ArrayPolar.errors: Overlapping objects with high count + 360°. Missing selection fails silently. Invalid center point coordinates.

-ArrayLinear.quick: -ArrayLinear requires selection first | Vector mode: count then direction/distance | Two-point mode: count then two reference points

contexts.vector_mode: Use when you know exact direction and spacing. Vector magnitude determines distance between copies. Format: -ArrayLinear [count] [x,y,z]. Example: -ArrayLinear 5 10,0,0 creates 5 copies spaced 10 units apart in X direction.
contexts.two_point_mode: Use when you want to define spacing visually with reference points. Distance between points becomes the spacing interval. Format: -ArrayLinear [count] [point1] [point2]. Useful for matching existing geometry spacing.
contexts.default: Interactive mode prompts for all parameters step by step. Good for exploratory work where you want to see spacing before committing. Will ask for count, then direction method (vector or two points).

-ArrayLinear.errors: Fails if no objects selected beforehand | Invalid vector format causes parameter errors | Zero-length vectors or coincident points create no spacing

-Divide.quick: -Divide [curve] [count] | Creates count-1 point objects at equal divisions

contexts.parametric_modeling: Use division points as reference for array patterns, construction geometry, or parametric relationships. Points become independent objects for downstream operations.
contexts.construction_lines: Division points serve as snap targets for construction geometry. Combine with Point object snaps for precise geometric construction workflows.
contexts.curve_analysis: Provides equal parameter spacing along curves for analysis or measurement. Useful for checking curve uniformity or creating measurement references.

-Divide.errors: Fails on invalid curves, zero/negative divisions. Points may cluster on short curves or appear sparse on long ones.

-Split.quick: -Split: Breaks objects into components. Requires selection first.

contexts.default: Splits selected objects into separate parts using default parameters. Use _SelPrev to work with previously selected objects.

-Split.errors: Fails if no objects selected or geometry not splittable

-Cap.quick: -Cap: Creates planar caps on open edges. Only works if edges are planar and within tolerance.

contexts.modeling: Essential for closing open surfaces/polysurfaces. Use after Boolean operations or surface trimming that leaves holes. Check edge planarity first - use PlanarSrf for complex openings.
contexts.mesh_repair: Caps planar openings in meshes. Useful for 3D printing prep. May need to convert mesh to NURBS first for better results. Check mesh normals after capping.
contexts.surface_finishing: Final step in surface modeling workflows. JoinResult=Yes creates single polysurface. DeleteInput=No preserves originals for comparison. Adjust tolerance for precision control.

-Cap.errors: Fails on non-planar edges, misaligned vertices, or tolerance issues. 'Cannot cap' means opening isn't planar - use Patch or manual surface creation instead.

-OffsetSrf.quick: _-OffsetSrf surface distance | Direction follows surface normal - may go inward unexpectedly

contexts.modeling: Creates parallel surfaces at specified distance. Use 'solid' option for closed surfaces to create thickness. 'bothsides' creates offsets in both directions simultaneously.
contexts.fabrication: Generates material thickness or clearance surfaces. Check offset direction carefully - positive/negative relative to surface normal, not visual expectation.
contexts.analysis: Produces equidistant surfaces for clearance studies. Corner handling affects intersection behavior - Sharp/Round/Smooth options control edge treatment.

-OffsetSrf.errors: Complex surfaces fail offset operations. Very small distances hit tolerance limits. Large offsets on curved surfaces create self-intersections.

-ExtrudeSrf.quick: _-ExtrudeSrf: Select surface → specify direction/distance. Open surfaces = extruded surface, closed = solid.

contexts.solid_creation: Use closed surfaces for solids. Open surfaces only create extruded surfaces. Check surface closure with What command first.
contexts.direction_control: Direction can be vector, distance value, or BothSides option. Tapered option adds draft angle for manufacturing.
contexts.automation: Requires surface selection first. Use _SelLast or pre-select. DeleteInput removes original surface automatically.

-ExtrudeSrf.errors: Complex surfaces fail to extrude - simplify first. Tiny distances invisible. Missing direction prompts user input.

contexts.type=line: _-Extend _SelPrev _Type=Line 10 - creates straight extensions regardless of curve type
contexts.default: _-Extend 5 _SelLast - extends by distance with default smooth continuation
contexts.to_surface: _-Extend {selection} _ToSurface - extends curve until it intersects target surface

-Extend.errors: Non-extendable curves fail silently | Negative distance trims | ToSurface fails if no intersection possible

-SimplifyCrv.quick: -SimplifyCrv: Reduces curve control points within tolerance. Critical: backup originals, check tolerance carefully.

contexts.cleanup: Use after importing curves with excessive control points. Start with loose tolerance, tighten gradually until acceptable quality.
contexts.optimization: Reduces file size and improves performance. Essential before manufacturing or when curves cause display lag.
contexts.preparation: Apply before using curves for surfaces or solids. Simplified curves often work better with downstream operations.

-SimplifyCrv.errors: High tolerance destroys curve shape. Complex curves may not simplify if already optimal. Always verify against original.

-Dot.quick: _-Dot [text] x,y,z - Creates text dot annotation. Parameter order matters: text first, then coordinates.

contexts.modeling: Quick point labeling during design. Use meaningful labels like 'corner1' or 'center'. Dots stay visible at all zoom levels.
contexts.documentation: Mark key points for drawings. Text becomes part of annotation system. Consider label clarity for final output.
contexts.scripting: Reliable coordinate placement. Always specify text before coordinates to ensure creation. Good for automated point marking.

-Dot.errors: Wrong parameter order (coordinates first) may fail. Invalid coordinates cause placement errors. Empty text creates unlabeled dots.

-Leader.quick: _-Leader <start> <end> <text> | Underscore prefix required for command-line execution

contexts.annotation: Creates leader lines pointing to features with text labels. Use for callouts, dimensions, and object identification in technical drawings.
contexts.scripting: Command-line only with underscore prefix. Requires three parameters in sequence: start point, end point, then text string.
contexts.coordinate_input: Accepts 3D coordinates in x,y,z format. Can use object snaps or direct coordinate entry for precise placement.

-Leader.errors: Missing underscore prefix fails. Invalid coordinates cause prompts. Text parameter must be last.

-Dim.quick: Creates linear dimensions with _-Dim <point1> <point2> <dimension_line_location>. Command-line version requires exact coordinates.

contexts.default: Specify two extension line origins, then dimension line position. Use exact coordinates like 0,0,0 10,0,0 0,5,0 for precise placement.
contexts.continuous: Chain multiple dimensions by using 'continuous' option after first dimension is placed.
contexts.baseline: Create multiple dimensions from common baseline using 'baseline' option for consistent reference.
contexts.aligned: Use 'aligned' option to create dimensions that follow the angle of dimensioned objects.
contexts.rotated: Apply 'rotated' option to create dimensions at specific angles regardless of object orientation.

-Dim.errors: Fails with invalid coordinates or when dimension line location creates overlapping text. Dimension style must be set before command execution.

contexts.default: _-DimRadius _SelLast 10,0,0 - Select circular object, place dimension text. Fails silently on invalid geometry. Position text clearly away from other elements.

-DimRadius.errors: Silent failure on non-circular objects. Poor placement makes dimensions unreadable.

-DimDiameter.quick: Creates diameter dimension for circles/arcs. Syntax: _-DimDiameter. Only works on circular geometry.

contexts.modeling: Dimensions circular features in technical drawings. Click circle/arc then placement point for dimension line position.
contexts.drafting: Standard diameter annotation tool. Placement point controls both dimension line location and text position.
contexts.automation: Use _SelLast to dimension most recently created circle/arc. Requires visible circular geometry to select.

-DimDiameter.errors: Fails on non-circular curves, ellipses, or splines. Selection must be valid circle or arc geometry.

-Zoom.quick: _-Zoom _Extents | _Selected requires selection first | _Factor <1 zooms out, >1 zooms in

contexts.extents: Use _Extents for all visible objects, _All includes hidden (may zoom to distant geometry making visible tiny)
contexts.selected: Must select objects first or command has no effect. Good for focusing on specific geometry
contexts.target: Centers view on specified point without changing zoom level. Useful for navigation
contexts.factor: Multiplies current zoom: 0.5 halves view, 2 doubles it. More precise than In/Out
contexts.precision: _1To1 sets actual size scale. Factor mode gives exact control over zoom level

-Zoom.errors: _Selected with no selection does nothing. _All may zoom to hidden objects making scene appear empty

-ViewportProperties.quick: Sets viewport camera properties. Syntax: -ViewportProperties _Mode [params]. Camera/target must be different points.

contexts.CameraTarget: Sets camera position and target point. Use 3D coordinates like 50,50,30 0,0,0. Camera and target must be different locations to avoid errors.
contexts.Lens: Sets focal length in millimeters for perspective views only. Range typically 10-200mm. Very small/large values create unusable views.
contexts.Projection: Switches between Perspective (vanishing points) and Parallel (no distortion). Lens setting only affects perspective mode.

-ViewportProperties.errors: Fails if camera equals target point. Lens changes ignored in parallel projection. Extreme focal lengths create distorted/unusable views.

contexts.save: Captures current viewport state including position, zoom, rotation. Name required, must be unique in document.
contexts.restore: Applies saved view to active viewport. View must exist or command fails. Restores exact camera position.
contexts.list: Shows all named views in current document. No parameters needed. Useful for checking existing view names.
contexts.delete: Permanently removes named view. Requires _Yes confirmation. Cannot be undone once deleted.

-NamedView.errors: Fails if view name doesn't exist for restore/delete, name conflicts on save, invalid characters in names

contexts.world: Sets view relative to world coordinates - consistent regardless of construction plane orientation
contexts.cplane: Sets view relative to current construction plane - orientation depends on active CPlane setup

-SetView.errors: Missing dash shows dialogs; affects only active viewport in layouts

contexts.coordinate: Pan to specific x,y coordinates relative to current view orientation. May behave unexpectedly in perspective views.
contexts.directional: Use _Left, _Right, _Up, _Down for fixed increment movement. Consistent across all view types.
contexts.default: Default 0,0 coordinate pan. Useful for centering view or resetting pan position.

-Pan.errors: Won't zoom - use Zoom commands instead. Coordinates relative to view, not world space.

contexts.directional: Use _Left/_Right for horizontal rotation, _Up/_Down for vertical. Default angles vary by direction.
contexts.custom_angle: Specify _Angle=<degrees> before direction for precise control. Example: _-RotateView _Angle=45 _Left
contexts.incremental: Use small angles (15-30°) to avoid disorientation. Large rotations can cause confusing view changes.
contexts.multi_viewport: Only rotates the currently active viewport. Switch viewports before rotating if needed.

-RotateView.errors: Rotation is relative to current view, not world coordinates. Large angles cause disorienting jumps.

-PointLight.quick: Syntax: _-PointLight x,y,z | Creates invisible light object (objects_created=0)

contexts.coordinate_input: Direct coordinate specification in world space. Example: _-PointLight 0,0,10 places light 10 units above origin
contexts.default: Standard point light creation at specified 3D location. Light affects rendering but creates no visible geometry

-PointLight.errors: Invalid coordinates cause failure. Light invisible in wireframe views, only affects rendered output

contexts.default: Creates spotlight from light position to target. Beam angle (inner cone) must be smaller than field angle (outer cone). Position order: light first, then target. Use for directional lighting effects in rendering.

-SpotLight.errors: Fails if light and target positions are identical (no direction). Beam angle > field angle creates invalid cone geometry.

-DirectionalLight.quick: Creates parallel light rays from direction. Syntax: -DirectionalLight <vector> | Critical: Direction points FROM origin TO vector

contexts.direction_vector: Single vector mode: -DirectionalLight 0,0,-1 creates downward light. Use normalized vectors for predictable intensity and direction.
contexts.two_point: Two-point mode: -DirectionalLight 0,0,10 0,0,0 creates light from high to low. More intuitive than vector mode for positioning.
contexts.default: Default downward light: -DirectionalLight 0,0,-1. Good for general scene illumination simulating overhead lighting.

-DirectionalLight.errors: Fails silently without rendering enabled. No visual feedback in wireframe views. Multiple lights cause overexposure.

contexts.default: Creates linear light between two points. Light direction flows from start to end point. Only visible in rendered viewports or during actual rendering.

-LinearLight.errors: Light appears invisible in wireframe/shaded modes. Switch to rendered viewport to see effect.

-Mesh.quick: _-Mesh converts surfaces to polygonal mesh. High density = large files, low density = lost detail.

contexts.default: _-Mesh _SelPrev for basic conversion. Density 0.0-1.0 controls polygon count. Good for simple surfaces needing mesh format.
contexts.detailed_options: _-Mesh _SelPrev _DetailedOptions for complex surfaces. Control angle tolerance, edge length. Essential for curved/organic geometry requiring quality mesh.
contexts.performance: High density creates large files impacting performance. Start with lower density, increase only if detail loss unacceptable. Monitor file size growth.

-Mesh.errors: Fails without surface/solid selection. One-way conversion - no automatic NURBS recovery. Complex surfaces need DetailedOptions or poor quality results.

contexts.corner: Default: two base corners + height. Height always goes in Z direction from base plane.
contexts.center: Center point + corner for orientation + height. Corner defines box orientation, not just size.
contexts.diagonal: Two opposite corners of complete 3D box. Don't use base corners - specify full volume endpoints.

-MeshBox.errors: Diagonal mode fails with base corners only. Center mode needs orientation corner, not dimensions.

contexts.default: _-MeshSphere {center} {radius} - standard triangular mesh topology

-MeshSphere.errors: Different from NURBS Sphere - limited editing options

contexts.default: Standard: center point, radius, height. Creates polygon mesh cylinder around Z-axis from base center.
contexts.2point: Axis mode: first point, second point, radius. Cylinder height = distance between points, oriented along axis.

-MeshCylinder.errors: Radius must be positive. Creates mesh not NURBS - no conversion to surfaces.

-MeshCone.quick: -MeshCone base_center radius height|apex_point | DirectionConstraint=None for free orientation

contexts.vertical: Default mode: -MeshCone 0,0,0 5 10 creates vertical cone with height along Z-axis, base in XY plane
contexts.free_direction: -MeshCone _DirectionConstraint=None 0,0,0 5 0,0,10 uses apex point for both height and orientation instead of vertical constraint
contexts.modeling: Creates mesh primitive cone for quick geometry blocking, use Cone command for NURBS surfaces instead
contexts.scripting: Third parameter changes meaning: height in default mode vs apex point with DirectionConstraint=None

-MeshCone.errors: Forgetting DirectionConstraint=None when wanting non-vertical cone, confusing height vs apex point parameters

contexts.corner: Default mode: _-MeshPlane <corner1> <corner2> creates rectangular mesh aligned to axes
contexts.center: _Center mode: center point then corner defines both size and orientation of mesh plane
contexts.3point: _3Point mode: three non-collinear points define arbitrary orientation mesh plane

-MeshPlane.errors: Collinear points in 3Point fail | Invalid coordinates reject | Missing corner point prompts

contexts.default: Creates horizontal torus mesh. Center point defines position, major radius is center-to-tube distance, minor radius is tube thickness. No vertical orientation option available.

-MeshTorus.errors: Major radius must exceed minor radius. Equal radii create sphere-like shape, very small minor radius creates thin ring.

-QuadRemesh.quick: _-QuadRemesh mesh → quad-dominant topology | Loses original UV mapping

contexts.default: Interactive remeshing with target quad count and adaptive sizing options. Use _SelPrev for previously selected meshes. Consider mesh complexity vs processing time.

-QuadRemesh.errors: Fails on NURBS/non-mesh objects. Large meshes cause long processing times. Unreasonable quad counts lose detail.

-Camera.quick: -Camera Show displays viewport camera info | Must use dash prefix

contexts.show: Shows camera properties for active viewport including position, target, lens length, and field of view. Useful for documenting or troubleshooting view settings.

-Camera.errors: May not work in orthographic views, only perspective | Info shown is viewport-specific

-SetCamera.quick: _-SetCamera | No prompts, uses defaults | May fail without established camera position

contexts.scripting: Perfect for automated camera positioning in scripts - no user interaction required, immediate execution
contexts.modeling: Quick camera reset during modeling workflow - instant positioning without dialog interruption
contexts.presentation: Rapid viewport changes for presentations - consistent camera positioning without manual input

-SetCamera.errors: Fails silently if no default camera exists | Immediate viewport change may disorient users | Cannot interactively adjust settings

-Turntable.quick: _-Turntable starts continuous viewport rotation around view center. Press Esc to stop.

contexts.presentation: Ideal for showcasing 3D models - creates smooth 360° rotation for client presentations or documentation
contexts.modeling: Useful for inspecting geometry from all angles while working - helps spot issues or plan next steps
contexts.performance: May slow down complex scenes - consider hiding unnecessary objects before starting animation

-Turntable.errors: Runs indefinitely until stopped manually. Heavy scenes may stutter or lag during rotation.

-SelAll.quick: -SelAll | Selects all visible objects, replaces current selection

contexts.modeling: Quick way to select entire model for operations like scale, move, or copy. Useful before grouping or applying materials to everything.
contexts.cleanup: Essential for mass operations like purging unused materials, checking object properties, or preparing files for export.
contexts.layer_management: Selects all objects on visible/unlocked layers only. Hidden or locked layer objects remain unselected regardless of visibility.

-SelAll.errors: Nothing selected if all objects are hidden/locked. Replaces existing selection without warning.

-SelNone.quick: -SelNone | Clears all selections instantly. Cannot undo - must reselect manually.

contexts.scripting: Use before operations requiring no selection. Executes immediately without prompts.
contexts.modeling: Quick way to start fresh when selection becomes complex or unwieldy.
contexts.cleanup: Essential for clearing selections before automated workflows or batch operations.

-SelNone.errors: No typical errors - always executes. Risk: accidentally clearing complex selections that are hard to recreate.

-SelLast.quick: Syntax: -SelLast | Selects most recently created object | Gotcha: Creation order, not modification order

contexts.modeling: Essential for selecting newly created geometry without knowing object names. Useful after complex operations to verify what was just made.
contexts.scripting: Reliable way to capture the result of the last creation command. Combine with object queries to verify selection success.
contexts.import: Imported objects follow file order - last imported object becomes selectable. Useful for processing batch imports sequentially.

-SelLast.errors: Fails silently if no objects exist. Arrays/groups may have unpredictable last selection behavior.

-SelPrev.quick: Restores previous selection state. Only works if there was a prior selection.

contexts.default: Immediately restores the selection that was active before current selection. No dialogue or options - executes instantly when called.

-SelPrev.errors: Fails silently if no previous selection exists or if previously selected objects were deleted.

-Invert.quick: _-Invert | Flips selection: selected→unselected, unselected→selected | Hidden objects may become selected

contexts.default: _-Invert executes immediately with no dialogue. Affects all objects in document including hidden ones. Locked objects/layers remain unchanged. If nothing selected, everything becomes selected.

-Invert.errors: No syntax errors possible. May unexpectedly select many hidden objects if large model with nothing initially selected.

-SelCrv.quick: _-SelCrv | Selects ALL curves in model, replaces current selection

contexts.scripting: Use before operations needing all curves selected. No parameters needed, immediate execution.
contexts.cleanup: Quick way to select all curves for deletion, modification, or layer changes.
contexts.filtering: Combine with Invert to select everything except curves, or use SelAdd variants for additive selection.

-SelCrv.errors: Silently selects nothing if no curves exist. Always replaces current selection.

-SelClosedCrv.quick: _-SelClosedCrv | Selects ALL closed curves - no filter control

contexts.default: Auto-selects all closed curves (circles, ellipses, closed polylines/splines) in document. No user interaction. Check status bar for selection count.

-SelClosedCrv.errors: May select unwanted curves on all layers. No undo for selection itself.

-SelOpenCrv.quick: _-SelOpenCrv | Selects ALL open curves instantly - no prompts, no filtering

contexts.cleanup: Use after importing/modeling to identify incomplete geometry. Pair with SelNone to clear first if needed.
contexts.validation: Quick check for unclosed curves that might cause surface/solid creation failures.
contexts.filtering: No type filtering - selects lines, polylines, splines equally. Use specific Sel commands for targeted selection.

-SelOpenCrv.errors: May select hundreds of curves unexpectedly. No undo for selection itself, but operations on selected curves are undoable.

contexts.scripting: Use before surface operations to ensure all surfaces are selected. Clears previous selection automatically.
contexts.modeling: Quick way to select all surfaces for global operations like hide, lock, or property changes.
contexts.cleanup: Useful for identifying all surface geometry in complex models before conversion or analysis.

-SelSrf.errors: No surfaces = empty selection. Hidden surfaces still selected.

contexts.default: _-SelPolysrf executes immediately with no dialogue. Selects only polysurface objects, ignoring individual surfaces or other geometry types. Use after creating complex models to isolate multi-surface objects.

-SelPolysrf.errors: Selects nothing if no polysurfaces exist. Won't select individual surfaces within polysurfaces.

-SelClosedPolysrf.quick: _-SelClosedPolysrf | Selects all closed polysurfaces. Single surfaces won't be selected even if closed.

contexts.modeling: Use after boolean operations to verify which objects are properly closed volumes. Helpful for identifying watertight geometry.
contexts.preparation: Essential before 3D printing or analysis - ensures only sealed objects are selected for export or further processing.
contexts.cleanup: Quick way to isolate closed polysurfaces from mixed geometry when organizing models or separating solid from surface objects.

-SelClosedPolysrf.errors: May select nothing if no closed polysurfaces exist. Won't select single surfaces or polysurfaces with gaps/openings.

-SelLayer.quick: _-SelLayer LayerName | Case-sensitive names, clears previous selection

contexts.batch_operations: Select all objects on specific layers for bulk modifications like material assignment or property changes
contexts.layer_management: Quickly isolate objects by layer for visibility control or organizational tasks
contexts.wildcard_selection: Use * and ? patterns to select multiple layers at once (e.g., 'Wall*' selects Wall01, Wall02, etc.)

-SelLayer.errors: Case mismatch fails silently, hidden layers ignored, locked objects selected but unmodifiable

-SelColor.quick: -SelColor [R,G,B] | Exact RGB match only - materials affect results

contexts.default: Selects objects by exact RGB color match. Use 255,0,0 format or interactive picker. Material colors may differ from display colors.

-SelColor.errors: Fails on approximate colors, material vs object color confusion, layer color inheritance issues

contexts.cleanup: Use -SelName * to deselect all objects, or -SelName temp* to remove temporary objects from selection
contexts.filtering: Combine with other selection commands: select group, then -SelName unwanted* to refine selection
contexts.workflow: Useful after SelAll when you want to exclude specific named objects from bulk operations

-SelName.errors: Wrong direction: adds instead of removes | No wildcards: exact match only

-SelDup.quick: -SelDup | Selects geometric duplicates | May select more than expected with loose tolerance

contexts.cleanup: Essential for model cleanup - finds duplicate geometry for deletion. Check selection count before deleting to avoid removing too much.
contexts.analysis: Useful for identifying redundant geometry in imported models or after array operations. Combine with properties panel to verify duplicates.
contexts.optimization: Part of file size reduction workflow. Use before Purge command to remove unnecessary duplicate objects from model.

-SelDup.errors: Tolerance too loose selects similar objects | Misses duplicates with tiny differences | Properties differ but geometry same

-SelSmall.quick: -SelSmall {tolerance} | Watch tolerance - too high selects wanted objects

contexts.cleanup: Use after importing/modeling to find tiny leftover geometry. Start with very small tolerance (0.001) and increase gradually until you see selections.
contexts.model_prep: Before final output, check for micro-objects that could cause issues. Consider model units - what's 'small' in mm vs inches differs greatly.
contexts.troubleshooting: If nothing selects, tolerance may be too small. If everything selects, tolerance is too large. Hidden/locked objects also get selected if they meet criteria.

-SelSmall.errors: No selection with tiny tolerance | Everything selected with large tolerance | Accidentally selecting important small details

-SelBadObjects.quick: -SelBadObjects | Selects invalid geometry automatically | Check selection count first

contexts.model_cleanup: Essential for identifying problematic geometry before export or analysis. Run after importing files or complex operations. Follow with Check command for details.
contexts.troubleshooting: First step when experiencing display issues, crashes, or unexpected behavior. Bad objects often cause instability in downstream operations.
contexts.quality_control: Use before finalizing models or sending to fabrication. Combine with SelDup, SelSmall for comprehensive geometry validation.

-SelBadObjects.errors: May select hundreds of objects in corrupted files. Only identifies problems - doesn't fix them. Use repair commands like RebuildEdges afterward.

-SelBlockInstance.quick: _-SelBlockInstance - selects ALL block instances in model (may be more than intended)

contexts.default: No dialogue, automatically selects all block instances. Nested blocks selected at top level only. Command completes with no selection if no blocks exist.

-SelBlockInstance.errors: May select more blocks than intended if many exist in model

-SelGroup.quick: Deselects grouped objects from selection. Only affects objects in groups/blocks.

contexts.cleanup: Use after complex selections to isolate ungrouped geometry for individual operations while keeping grouped elements intact
contexts.modeling: Helpful when working with mixed selections of individual objects and grouped assemblies - removes groups to focus on loose geometry
contexts.organization: Part of selection refinement workflow when you need to separate grouped content from individual objects for different treatments

-SelGroup.errors: No effect if selection contains only ungrouped objects. Silent operation - no feedback when nothing changes.

-SelPt.quick: -SelPt selects all visible point objects, clearing existing selection

contexts.scripting: Use -SelPt for immediate selection without dialog. Use SelPt (no hyphen) to add to existing selection instead of replacing it
contexts.modeling: Quickly isolate all point objects for operations like moving, deleting, or changing properties. Points on hidden/locked layers won't be selected
contexts.cleanup: Efficient way to find and select all point objects in complex models for deletion or organization

-SelPt.errors: No points selected if all points are hidden or locked

-SelText.quick: -SelText: filters current selection to text objects only

contexts.filtering_workflow: Use after selecting mixed objects to isolate text for editing or formatting operations
contexts.text_management: Essential for bulk text operations - filter first, then apply changes to all selected text
contexts.cleanup_operations: Combine with Delete or Hide to remove all text from selected geometry groups

-SelText.errors: No effect if no selection exists; deselects non-text annotation objects like dimensions

-SelDim.quick: -SelDim | Selects all dimensions, clears existing selection

contexts.drafting: Essential for dimension management - quickly isolate all dimensions for editing, styling, or layer changes
contexts.cleanup: Use before dimension operations like changing text height, moving to specific layers, or deleting outdated dimensions
contexts.inspection: Fast way to verify dimension count and distribution across model before finalizing drawings

-SelDim.errors: Empty selection if no dimensions exist; clears current selection without warning

-SelHatch.quick: _-SelHatch | Selects ALL hatches instantly, including locked/hidden layers

contexts.default: _-SelHatch executes immediately without dialog. Selects every hatch object in the model regardless of layer visibility or lock status. No options available.

-SelHatch.errors: No hatches = empty selection but command succeeds. Cannot filter by layer or properties.

-SelLight.quick: -SelLight | Selects all visible light objects, clears existing selection

contexts.lighting_setup: Use to quickly select all lights for bulk operations like moving, copying, or property changes. Combine with Show/Hide commands to control which lights are selectable.
contexts.scene_cleanup: Efficient way to identify and manage all lighting in complex scenes. Follow with Delete or properties panel to modify multiple lights simultaneously.
contexts.rendering_prep: Quick selection of all lights before render setup. Use with Layer commands to organize lights or Properties to adjust intensity/color in batch.

-SelLight.errors: Hidden lights ignored. Empty selection if no lights exist. Clears current selection first.

-SelOpenPolysrf.quick: _-SelOpenPolysrf | Selects polysurfaces with naked edges | Clears existing selection first

contexts.modeling_cleanup: Essential for finding incomplete geometry during model validation. Use before joining operations to identify problem areas.
contexts.quality_control: Part of geometry checking workflow. Combine with ShowEdges to visualize naked edges on selected open polysurfaces.
contexts.preparation_for_operations: Select open polysurfaces before attempting joins or boolean operations that require closed geometry.

-SelOpenPolysrf.errors: Returns empty selection if no open polysurfaces exist. Won't select surfaces or meshes, only polysurfaces with naked edges.

-SelClosedSrf.quick: _-SelClosedSrf | Selects all mathematically closed surfaces, clears existing selection

contexts.modeling: Essential for identifying watertight surfaces before boolean operations or analysis. Polysurfaces selected as units if closed overall.
contexts.quality_check: Quick way to verify which surfaces form complete boundaries. Mathematical closure may differ from visual appearance.
contexts.selection_workflow: Clears current selection first, then adds all closed surfaces. Use before operations requiring watertight geometry.

-SelClosedSrf.errors: Visually closed surfaces may not select if mathematically open due to tolerance gaps or trimming issues

-SelOpenSrf.quick: _-SelOpenSrf | Selects all open surfaces automatically. Clears existing selection first.

contexts.modeling: Use to identify incomplete surfaces needing closure. Helpful for quality checks before boolean operations or mesh creation.
contexts.cleanup: Quick way to find surfaces with gaps or boundary edges that may cause downstream issues in manufacturing or analysis.
contexts.inspection: Combine with ShowEdges to visualize which surfaces have open boundaries versus closed ones.

-SelOpenSrf.errors: Only selects individual surfaces, not polysurfaces. May select surfaces with tiny invisible gaps.

-SelPlanarCrv.quick: _-SelPlanarCrv | Auto-selects all mathematically planar curves | Replaces current selection

contexts.cleanup: Quickly isolate planar curves for 2D operations or to separate from 3D space curves
contexts.validation: Check which curves in your model are truly planar vs slightly warped or 3D
contexts.workflow: Use before operations that require planar curves like certain extrusions or boolean operations

-SelPlanarCrv.errors: Slightly warped curves won't select even if they look flat | No selection in empty models

-SelLinearCrv.quick: _-SelLinearCrv | Only true linear curves, not polylines

contexts.default: _-SelLinearCrv runs silently, adds to selection. Excludes polylines and slight curves even if visually linear.

-SelLinearCrv.errors: Polylines won't select despite linear segments; arcs with large radii excluded; adds to existing selection

contexts.default: Instantly selects all polylines without prompts. Adds to existing selection - use SelNone first for clean selection. Ignores layer visibility/lock status.

-SelPolyline.errors: No direct failures - always runs but may select nothing if no polylines exist

-SelClippingPlane.quick: _-SelClippingPlane | Selects all clipping plane objects | Clears existing selection first

contexts.modeling: Use to quickly isolate clipping planes for editing properties or repositioning without affecting model geometry
contexts.documentation: Select clipping planes to check their names, layers, or export them separately from main geometry
contexts.cleanup: Identify all clipping planes in complex scenes for deletion or organization before finalizing models

-SelClippingPlane.errors: Silent completion if no clipping planes exist; doesn't select clipped geometry, only the plane objects themselves

-SelMesh.quick: -SelMesh | Selects all mesh objects, clears existing selection

contexts.modeling: Quick way to isolate mesh objects for operations like smoothing, subdivision, or conversion to NURBS
contexts.cleanup: Essential for identifying imported mesh geometry that may need conversion or deletion
contexts.analysis: Use before mesh analysis commands to work only with mesh objects in complex scenes

-SelMesh.errors: Empty selection if no meshes exist; clears current selection without warning

-SelClosedMesh.quick: Selects closed (watertight) mesh objects only. Requires no naked edges.
