contexts.mesh_analysis: Use before operations requiring watertight meshes like 3D printing or boolean operations. Quickly identifies which meshes are solid.
contexts.quality_control: Essential for validating mesh integrity in manufacturing workflows. Closed meshes indicate proper topology for downstream processes.
contexts.modeling_cleanup: Helps isolate problematic open meshes that need repair. Use with SelOpenMesh to categorize all mesh objects by closure state.

-SelClosedMesh.errors: Ignores NURBS/polysurfaces entirely. Tiny gaps exclude meshes from selection even if visually closed.

-SelOpenMesh.quick: _-SelOpenMesh | Selects all non-watertight mesh objects | Only meshes, not NURBS/polysurfs

contexts.mesh_analysis: Use before mesh repair workflows to identify problematic meshes. Combine with ShowEdges to visualize holes. Follow with MeshRepair for fixing.
contexts.quality_control: Part of mesh validation pipeline. Helps identify manufacturing issues or modeling errors. Use SelClosedMesh for comparison of good vs bad meshes.
contexts.batch_processing: Automates selection for mesh cleanup scripts. No user interaction required. Clear selection first if needed for accurate results.

-SelOpenMesh.errors: Won't select visually open NURBS surfaces. May miss meshes with micro-gaps that appear closed. Includes intentional openings you might want to keep.

-CurveBoolean.quick: Creates regions from closed planar curves with boolean operations. Syntax: _-CurveBoolean [points] or _AllRegions

contexts.allregions: Use _AllRegions to automatically process all detected closed curve regions without manual point selection
contexts.default: Click points inside closed curves to select specific regions. Points must be within valid closed curve boundaries
contexts.combineregions: Use _CombineRegions with options like _None to control how overlapping regions are merged together

-CurveBoolean.errors: Fails with open curves, non-coplanar curves, or points outside closed regions. May create zero objects if no valid intersections

-CurveThroughPt.quick: _-CurveThroughPt point1 point2 [more_points...] | Needs multiple points to create curve

contexts.default: Creates interpolated curve through specified points. Enter points sequentially, press Enter to finish. Minimum 2 points required for curve generation.
contexts.interpolate: Use _Interpolate option to specify interpolation method before entering points. Different methods (cubic, linear, etc.) create varying curve smoothness through same points.

-CurveThroughPt.errors: Single point fails - no curve created. Incomplete point entry leaves command hanging. Points too close may create degenerate curves.

-DeleteSubCrv.quick: _-DeleteSubCrv: Deletes curve portion between two points. Must select curve first, points must lie on curve.

contexts.default: Interactive selection: pick curve, then click start/end points on curve for deletion segment
contexts.with_coordinates: Automated deletion: _-DeleteSubCrv 0,0,0 10,0,0 - coordinates must correspond to actual curve locations
contexts.precision_modeling: Use object snaps or exact coordinates to ensure deletion points align with curve geometry
contexts.batch_operations: Combine with selection filters to process multiple curves, verify each curve has valid deletion segment

-DeleteSubCrv.errors: Fails if points don't lie on curve, wrong selection type, or invalid coordinate format

-ExtractSubCrv.quick: Syntax: _-ExtractSubCrv [point1] [point2] | Must select curve first, points must lie on/near curve

contexts.default: Interactive mode: select curve, then specify start/end points via coordinates or picking. Extracted portion becomes new curve object while original remains unchanged.

-ExtractSubCrv.errors: Fails silently with no curve selected. Points off curve cause extraction failure. Ensure curve selection before point specification.

-ExtrudeCrvAlongCrv.quick: Extrudes profile curve along path curve. Profile/path must be separate curves.

contexts.modeling: Creates surfaces from curve profiles following complex paths. Useful for railings, moldings, pipes along routes.
contexts.architectural: Generate trim profiles, handrails, or decorative elements that follow building contours or curved paths.
contexts.product_design: Create swept features like handles, tubes, or complex extrusions that follow non-linear paths.

-ExtrudeCrvAlongCrv.errors: Fails with same curve as profile/path, self-intersecting paths, or misaligned curve orientations.

-ExtrudeSrfAlongCrv.quick: Extrudes surface along curve path. Syntax: _-ExtrudeSrfAlongCrv. Critical: curve position/direction affects result.

contexts.architectural: Perfect for creating moldings, trim, handrails along curved paths. Use Cap=Flat for clean connections to walls.
contexts.mechanical: Create complex housings, tubes, conduits following curved paths. CornerType=Sharp for precise mechanical fits.
contexts.product_design: Generate organic forms, handles, decorative elements. Use Simplify=Yes to reduce surface complexity.
contexts.jewelry: Form bands, settings, decorative elements along curved paths. Watch tolerances with small geometry.

-ExtrudeSrfAlongCrv.errors: Fails with self-intersecting curves, misaligned surface/curve positioning, or extreme scale differences between inputs.

-FilletCorners.quick: _-FilletCorners [radius] | Requires sharp vertices, fails if radius too large for segments

contexts.polyline_editing: Works on polyline corners with sharp angles. Use reasonable radius relative to segment lengths. Join option creates single continuous curve.
contexts.curve_modification: Only affects sharp vertices, not smooth sections. Trim option controls how segments meet fillet. May fail on closed curves with problematic corner configurations.
contexts.precision_modeling: Fillet radius must be positive and scaled appropriately to geometry. Large radii can exceed adjacent segment lengths causing command failure.

-FilletCorners.errors: Fails when radius exceeds segment length, no sharp corners exist, or closed curve geometry conflicts

-FilletSrfCrv.quick: _-FilletSrfCrv surface curve radius | Check proximity & scale

contexts.modeling: Creates smooth transitions between surfaces and curves. Essential for organic forms and mechanical parts requiring rounded edges. Radius must match geometry scale.
contexts.precision: Fillet radius critical - too large fails, too small creates tiny surfaces. Position curve near surface edge for best results. Check tangency requirements.
contexts.workflow: Often used after surface creation to add detail. Trim=Yes removes original geometry, Join=Yes creates single object. Test radius on simple geometry first.

-FilletSrfCrv.errors: Fails if curve too far from surface, radius too large for geometry, or complex intersections exist

-FitCrv.quick: _-FitCrv [tolerance] | Select objects first | Balance tolerance: too small=complex, too large=poor fit

contexts.point_fitting: Best for fitting curves through scattered points or digitized data. Use moderate tolerance (0.01-0.1) to balance smoothness vs accuracy.
contexts.curve_simplification: Reduces control points in existing curves. Start with larger tolerance and decrease until acceptable quality. Compare original vs fitted curve.
contexts.reverse_engineering: Recreate curves from mesh edges or imported geometry. Very small tolerance needed for precision work, but may create heavy curves.
contexts.data_cleanup: Remove noise from measured or scanned curve data. Tolerance should be slightly larger than expected measurement error.

-FitCrv.errors: Fails with no selection or invalid geometry types. Extremely small tolerance crashes or hangs. Large tolerance may fail to converge.

-InsertLineIntoCrv.quick: Syntax: _-InsertLineIntoCrv | Critical: Insertion point must lie exactly on the selected curve

contexts.curve_editing: Modifies existing curve geometry by inserting line segment at specified point. Changes curve parameterization and may affect downstream operations that depend on original curve structure.
contexts.design_workflow: Useful for adding linear segments to smooth curves for manufacturing constraints or design requirements. Consider using InsertKnot for maintaining curve type instead of geometric modification.
contexts.precision_modeling: Insertion point precision is critical - use object snaps or curve analysis tools to ensure accurate placement. Line direction and length directly affect resulting curve quality and continuity.

-InsertLineIntoCrv.errors: Fails if insertion point not on curve, invalid curve selection, or line parameters create self-intersecting geometry

-SelSelfIntersectingCrv.quick: _-SelSelfIntersectingCrv | Clears selection, finds curves crossing themselves

contexts.cleanup: Essential for finding problematic curves before operations like lofting or sweeping that fail on self-intersecting geometry
contexts.validation: Use after importing CAD files or creating complex curves to identify geometry issues that could cause downstream problems
contexts.troubleshooting: When commands fail unexpectedly on curves, run this to check if self-intersections are the cause

-SelSelfIntersectingCrv.errors: Misses tiny intersections below tolerance; doesn't detect visual overlaps that aren't true intersections

-SelShortCrv.quick: Selects curves shorter than specified length. Syntax: _-SelShortCrv {length}. Units must match document units.

contexts.cleanup: Remove tiny curve segments by selecting with very small threshold (0.001) then deleting selected objects.
contexts.filtering: Use before operations that need curves above certain size - select short ones first to exclude them.
contexts.quality_control: Check model for unintended micro-curves that could cause downstream issues in manufacturing.

-SelShortCrv.errors: Threshold too small selects nothing, too large selects all curves. Only works on curve objects, ignores surfaces/solids.

-SelSubDFriendlyCrv.quick: Selects curves compatible with SubD workflows. No options, operates on all visible curves.

contexts.subd_modeling: Essential for identifying which curves can be used as SubD cage edges or control curves. Helps prepare geometry for subdivision surface workflows.
contexts.curve_filtering: Part of selection filtering workflow. Use before converting to SubD or when cleaning up geometry for subdivision modeling.
contexts.quality_control: Identifies curves that meet SubD compatibility standards. Useful for validating imported geometry or checking curve quality.

-SelSubDFriendlyCrv.errors: Returns empty selection if no SubD-compatible curves exist. Ignores hidden curves and locked layers.

-MergeCrv.quick: _-MergeCrv _SelAll | Joins curve segments at coincident endpoints into continuous curves

contexts.cleanup: Essential for cleaning up imported CAD files with fragmented curves. Use after exploding complex geometry or importing from other formats.
contexts.modeling: Prepare curves for operations like sweep, loft, or extrude that require continuous input curves. Critical before using curves as rails or profiles.
contexts.scripting: Always use _SelAll or specific selection methods. Consider tolerance settings for precision work - default may be too loose for small geometry.

-MergeCrv.errors: Fails silently if endpoints exceed tolerance distance. Closed curves won't merge. Direction follows first selected curve, potentially reversing expected flow.

-SubCrv.quick: -SubCrv: Subtracts curves from objects. Curves must be closed, targets must be solid/surface.

contexts.default: Select target objects first, then curves to subtract. Use DeleteInput to remove original curves. ExtrudeCurves option available for 2D workflows.

-SubCrv.errors: Fails with open curves, non-solid targets, or non-intersecting geometry. Check curve closure and positioning.

-TweenCurves.quick: _-TweenCurves [number] | Requires exactly 2 curves, similar topology essential

contexts.modeling: Creates smooth transitions between profile curves for organic shapes. Use consistent curve directions and similar point counts for predictable results.
contexts.surface_prep: Generates intermediate curves for lofting operations. Match parameterization option improves surface quality when curves have different structures.
contexts.animation: Builds curve sequences for morphing animations. Keep curve complexity similar to avoid interpolation artifacts in downstream applications.

-TweenCurves.errors: Fails with dissimilar curve structures, opposite directions, or extreme parameter differences

-SlopeCrv.quick: -SlopeCrv disables slope curve display. Use SlopeCrv (no dash) to enable.

contexts.surface_analysis: Turns off slope curve visualization on surfaces. Use when slope display interferes with other analysis or viewport performance.
contexts.modeling_cleanup: Disables slope curve overlays to clean up viewport display. Helpful when working with complex surfaces where curves obstruct view.
contexts.performance: Removes slope curve calculations and display to improve viewport refresh rates on complex models.

-SlopeCrv.errors: No visible feedback when disabling. Won't work if slope curves weren't already enabled.

-OrientOnCrv.quick: Orients objects to align with curve. Syntax: -OrientOnCrv [objects] [ref_point] [target_point] _Enter

contexts.copy_mode: Use Copy option to duplicate while orienting. Original stays in place, oriented copy placed on curve.
contexts.scaling_mode: Scale option allows proportional adjustment during orientation to match curve characteristics.
contexts.precision_work: Reference points must be exact for proper alignment. Use object snaps for accuracy on both source and target.

-OrientOnCrv.errors: Fails with complex/discontinuous curves. Requires pre-selected objects and existing target curve in model space.

-Align.quick: -Align: Point-to-point alignment. Order matters - match source to target sequence.

contexts.default: Select objects, pick reference points on source, then corresponding target points. Use Copy option to preserve originals.
contexts.precision_work: Ensure clear, accessible reference points. Consider using object snaps for accuracy. Scale option available for size matching.
contexts.batch_operations: Use _SelLast for quick alignment of recently created objects. Consider grouping similar alignments together.

-Align.errors: Fails with unclear reference points or mismatched point sequences. Objects jump unexpectedly if point order is wrong.

-Bend.quick: -Bend removes bending from objects with bend history. Requires previous Bend command usage.

contexts.default: Interactive dialogue guides unbending process. Select objects previously modified with Bend command. Cannot fully automate due to required user interaction.

-Bend.errors: Fails on objects without bend history. May not perfectly restore original geometry if multiple transforms applied post-bend.

-BoxEdit.quick: _-BoxEdit disables box editing mode | Only works if mode is active

contexts.modeling: Use after BoxEdit to return objects to normal editing state. Essential for workflow cleanup when switching between box and point editing modes.
contexts.scripting: Silent execution with no feedback. Check if BoxEdit mode was active before calling. Useful in automated workflows to ensure clean object states.

-BoxEdit.errors: No effect if box editing wasn't active. No error message or confirmation when executed.

-BringForward.quick: Moves objects backward in display order (opposite of BringForward due to dash prefix)

contexts.overlapping_objects: Use when objects overlap and you need to change which appears on top. Effects only visible in shaded views, not wireframe.
contexts.layer_management: Alternative to layer ordering for quick depth adjustments. Affects display order within the same layer.
contexts.with_sellast: Use _SelLast option to immediately adjust newly created objects without manual selection.

-BringForward.errors: No visual change if objects don't overlap or in wireframe view. Requires object selection first.

-BringToFront.quick: -BringToFront | Moves objects to front of display order | Only affects visual appearance, not geometry hierarchy

contexts.overlapping_objects: Use when objects overlap and you need specific ones visible on top. Combine with selection filters like _SelLast for efficiency.
contexts.technical_drawings: Essential for controlling line precedence in 2D drawings. May need to repeat after geometry changes.
contexts.presentation_views: Arrange elements for clear visual hierarchy. Remember display order is viewport-specific.

-BringToFront.errors: Fails silently if no objects selected. Changes invisible with identical colors/materials. Display order resets with some viewport operations.

-Cage.quick: Toggles cage control point display for objects with cage deformation applied

contexts.modeling: Use to show/hide cage control points when editing deformed objects. Essential for precise cage-based modeling workflows.
contexts.visualization: Toggle cage display to reduce visual clutter when not actively editing cage deformations. Helps focus on object geometry.
contexts.editing: Must have cage deformation already applied to objects. Use with CageEdit for active modification of cage control points.

-Cage.errors: No visible effect if no caged objects exist. Cage points may be hard to see when overlapping geometry.

-CageEdit.quick: -CageEdit: Deforms objects using manipulable control cage. Modifies originals, not copies.

contexts.modeling: Essential for organic shape modification. Create cage around object, then manipulate cage points to deform geometry smoothly.
contexts.precision: Use with restraint - aggressive cage manipulation causes unwanted distortion. Test on copies first.
contexts.workflow: Command-line version bypasses UI dialogs. Select objects first, then cage appears for manipulation.

-CageEdit.errors: Over-manipulation creates mesh distortion. Complex geometry may fail or produce unexpected results.

-Distribute.quick: _-Distribute: Select objects first, then choose AlongCurve/Linear distribution method

contexts.linear_spacing: Use Linear with Distance option for precise spacing between two points. Number option divides the distance evenly among objects.
contexts.curve_distribution: AlongCurve requires selecting a curve after objects. Objects are positioned at equal parameter intervals along the curve path.

contexts.object_orientation: Objects maintain their original orientation during distribution. Use Orient command afterward if rotation is needed.

-Distribute.errors: Fails if no objects selected initially. AlongCurve fails without valid curve selection. Distance/Number conflicts require choosing one method.

-DragMode.quick: _-DragMode UVN|World|CPlane|View - Sets global drag behavior, affects all future moves

contexts.modeling: Use CPlane for predictable local moves, World for global positioning. UVN useful for surface-relative adjustments
contexts.precision: World mode gives consistent XYZ movement regardless of view angle. CPlane respects your working plane orientation
contexts.workflow: Set once at session start or when switching between 2D/3D work. Affects Move, Gumball, and all drag operations

-DragMode.errors: Unexpected movement directions when CPlane orientation differs from expectation. Mode persists globally until changed

-DragStrength.quick: _-DragStrength <value> | Sets drag deformation intensity (0-100) | Persists until changed

contexts.surface_editing: Controls how much surfaces deform during drag operations - start with moderate values (20-50) for predictable results
contexts.mesh_modeling: Higher values work better on dense meshes, lower values on simple surfaces - test incrementally to avoid extreme deformations
contexts.precision_work: Use low values (5-15) for subtle adjustments, disable with 0 when precise positioning needed without deformation

-DragStrength.errors: Extreme values cause uncontrollable deformation | Zero disables drag effects | Setting persists globally

-Flow.quick: -Flow: Fluid dynamics simulation on geometry. Requires closed surfaces/solids for proper boundaries.

contexts.cfd_analysis: Use closed solids as flow boundaries. Set proper units first - affects Reynolds numbers. Complex geometry = longer computation time.
contexts.boundary_setup: Select flow domain geometry with -Flow _SelLast. Ensure watertight surfaces to define inlet/outlet/wall boundaries correctly.
contexts.performance: Simplify geometry before analysis to reduce computation time. Use _SelPrev to rerun with modified parameters on same geometry.

-Flow.errors: Open surfaces fail boundary definition. Wrong units corrupt flow physics. Complex meshes timeout or crash.

-Gumball.quick: -Gumball | Utility command with hyphen prefix - runs non-interactively

contexts.default: Single execution utility function. Hyphen prefix ensures non-interactive mode. May not produce visible geometric results - likely system/plugin related functionality.

-Gumball.errors: Omitting hyphen changes behavior. May fail if expected plugin/system components unavailable.

contexts.default: Applies maelstrom transformation through interactive dialogue. Use _SelLast to auto-select recent objects. Multiple prompts require manual input - not fully scriptable without parameters.

-Maelstrom.errors: Fails without selection. May destroy original geometry. Cannot automate without parameter specification.

-Orient.quick: -Orient: Transform objects via 3-point coordinate systems. Order matters: source 3 points, then target 3 points.

contexts.precise_positioning: Use object snaps for accurate point selection. Consider using construction geometry to establish clear reference points for complex orientations.
contexts.architectural: Excellent for positioning building elements. Use grid intersections or known coordinates as reference points for consistent placement.
contexts.mechanical: Perfect for aligning parts in assemblies. Establish datum points on both source and target to ensure proper fit and orientation.

-Orient.errors: Objects vanish if oriented far from view. Wrong point order scrambles transformation. Missing snaps cause imprecise placement.

-Project.quick: -Project: Projects objects onto plane/surface. Avoid parallel directions to object.

contexts.cplane_projection: Use construction plane option for quick flattening to current CPlane. Maintains object relationships.
contexts.surface_projection: Select target surface first, then objects. Verify surface accessibility and normal orientation.
contexts.view_projection: Projects in current view direction. Useful for creating 2D representations from 3D models.
contexts.direction_vector: Specify exact direction with coordinates. Ensure vector is not parallel to projection plane.

-Project.errors: Fails with parallel projection directions, inaccessible targets, or degenerate geometry results.

-Pull.quick: -Pull: Move selected objects along direction/toward point | Must select objects first

contexts.modeling: Pull faces/edges to modify geometry. Direction vector controls uniform movement. Use with specific distance for precision.
contexts.transformation: Non-dialog version of Pull for scripting. Requires pre-selection. Direction affects all objects identically.
contexts.scripting: Batch pull operations without UI interruption. Combine with selection commands like _SelLast for automation.

-Pull.errors: Fails without selection. Direction conflicts with object constraints cause failures.

-ReleaseFromCage.quick: Releases objects from cage deformation control. Objects must be currently caged.

contexts.default: Select caged objects to release from deformation control. The cage remains but objects return to uncaged state. No interactive options available.

-ReleaseFromCage.errors: Fails if objects aren't under cage control. Released objects lose cage deformation permanently.

-SendBackward.quick: -SendBackward: Moves objects backward in display order. Requires selection, only visual effect.

contexts.default: Select objects first, then run command. Use _SelLast to automatically select most recent objects. Changes only affect visual layering when objects overlap in current view.

-SendBackward.errors: No visible change if objects don't overlap in view or in wireframe mode. Command fails without selection.

-SendToBack.quick: _-SendToBack _SelLast | Moves selected objects behind others in display order

contexts.overlapping_objects: Changes visual layering when objects overlap in view - affects display order only, not 3D position
contexts.selection_workflow: Requires pre-selected objects or use _SelLast to target most recent selection automatically
contexts.display_management: Part of drawing order commands - use with SendToFront, BringForward, SendBackward for layer control

-SendToBack.errors: Fails silently if no objects selected. Effect invisible if objects don't overlap in current view

-SetPt.quick: -SetPt: Move objects by base→target points | Needs selection first

contexts.precision_modeling: Use for exact point-to-point positioning when coordinates matter more than visual alignment
contexts.copy_operations: Add Copy option to duplicate at new location while keeping original in place
contexts.multiple_targets: Use Multiple option to place copies at several locations from same base point
contexts.object_alignment: Alternative to Move when you need precise point reference rather than distance/direction

-SetPt.errors: Fails without selection | Movement happens immediately after target point

-Shear.quick: -Shear: select objects > origin point > direction > angle/ratio. Origin placement critical for result.

contexts.modeling: Use Copy option to preserve originals when experimenting. Choose origin carefully - it's the anchor point that doesn't move during shear.
contexts.parametric: Shear transformations can break parametric relationships. Consider if maintaining history is important before applying.
contexts.precision: Use Ratio option for exact mathematical shearing. Angle mode uses degrees and may be more intuitive for visual adjustments.

-Shear.errors: Fails if shear direction equals shear axis. Complex curves may distort unexpectedly. Requires valid geometry selection.

-Smash.quick: -Smash breaks objects into fragments. Destructive - backup first.

contexts.default: Standard smash breaks selected objects into constituent parts or fragments. Use _SelLast/_SelAll for selection shortcuts. Operation is immediate after confirmation.

-Smash.errors: Destructive operation cannot be easily undone. Results vary by object type - some may not fragment as expected.

-Stretch.quick: -Stretch: Reverse stretch command. Requires selection first, interactive prompts for base point/direction/scale.

contexts.modeling: Use for inverse stretch operations on geometry. Select objects first, then specify base point and stretch parameters through interactive dialogue.
contexts.automation: Combine with _SelLast for scripting: '-Stretch _SelLast'. Handle interactive prompts programmatically for base point and scale factor.
contexts.troubleshooting: Minus prefix indicates alternative behavior vs standard Stretch. Ensure proper object selection before execution to avoid command failure.

-Stretch.errors: Fails without valid selection. Interactive dialogue can timeout. Dramatic geometry changes if wrong parameters entered.

-Taper.quick: -Taper: Select objects → specify axis → set scale factor. Dash bypasses UI dialogs.

contexts.modeling: Use for creating tapered forms like table legs, lamp bases, or architectural elements. Preview before accepting to avoid unwanted distortion.
contexts.scripting: Dash prefix ensures command-line operation without UI interruptions. Combine with _SelLast for automated workflows.
contexts.precision: Taper axis direction is critical - incorrect orientation produces unexpected results. Define base point carefully to control which end stays fixed.

-Taper.errors: Fails on unsupported geometry types. Extreme taper ratios cause severe distortion or invalid geometry.

-Twist.quick: -Twist: Select objects > axis start/end points > angle. Axis direction affects twist direction.

contexts.modeling: Progressive rotation along axis creates helical deformation. Use shorter axes for tighter twists, longer for gradual curves.
contexts.parametric: Twist angle distributes evenly along axis length. Consider axis placement for desired deformation center.
contexts.complex_geometry: Large angles risk self-intersection. Test with small increments on complex surfaces or solids.

-Twist.errors: Self-intersecting geometry from excessive angles. Wrong twist direction from reversed axis orientation.

-SetUserText.quick: Syntax: _-SetUserText [key] [value] | Keys are case-sensitive, overwrites existing

contexts.default: Select objects then enter key-value pairs. Use for custom metadata like material types, part numbers, or project info. Keys case-sensitive, values can be empty but avoid for clarity.

-SetUserText.errors: No selection fails silently. Case mismatches create duplicate keys. Empty values allowed but confusing later.

-GetUserText.quick: _-GetUserText: Retrieves user-defined text from selected objects. Objects must have user text attached.

contexts.default: Select objects with attached user text data. Command displays text key-value pairs but doesn't modify objects. Use _SelLast for quick access to recently modified objects.

-GetUserText.errors: Empty results if objects lack user text. Selection required - command fails without objects selected.

contexts.default: Sets document metadata key-value pairs. Use quotes for spaced keys/values. Overwrites existing keys. Case-sensitive key names.

-SetDocumentUserText.errors: Unquoted spaces break parsing. Key overwrites lose previous values.

-GetDocumentUserText.quick: _-GetDocumentUserText [key] | Case-sensitive keys | Returns nothing if key missing

contexts.scripting: Use for automated document metadata retrieval. Check return value for empty results before processing.
contexts.batch_processing: Omit key parameter to dump all entries for analysis. Parse output carefully as format may vary.
contexts.data_validation: Verify key existence before retrieval operations. Case sensitivity often causes lookup failures.

-GetDocumentUserText.errors: Silent failure on missing keys. No error message, just empty return. Case mismatch is common cause.

-SelUserText.quick: _-SelUserText | Selects objects with user text data. Clears existing selection first.

contexts.data_management: Use to find objects with custom metadata. Helpful for filtering objects by attached information before batch operations.
contexts.quality_control: Quickly identify which objects have documentation or custom properties attached. Useful for checking data completeness.
contexts.automation: Essential for scripts that need to process only objects with specific user text data. Combine with other selection filters.

-SelUserText.errors: Returns empty selection if no objects have user text. Won't select objects with only names/layer assignments.

contexts.new: Creates layer with optional color: _-Layer _New MyLayer _Color 255,0,0. Color values 0-255 RGB format.
contexts.set: Sets active layer for new objects: _-Layer _Set LayerName. Must exist first or command fails.
contexts.visibility: _On/_Off controls layer visibility. Hidden layers still exist, objects just not displayed.
contexts.locking: _Lock/_Unlock prevents/allows selection and modification. Locked objects visible but untouchable.

-Layer.errors: Non-existent layer names fail silently. Invalid color values (>255 or non-integer) rejected. Case mismatch causes failures.

-ChangeLayer.quick: _-ChangeLayer _SelLast TargetLayer | Target layer must exist first

contexts.default: Moves selected objects to specified layer. Objects keep all properties except layer. Use _SelLast for last created objects or select manually first.

-ChangeLayer.errors: Fails if target layer doesn't exist, is locked/frozen, or has spaces without quotes

-ChangeToCurrentLayer.quick: Moves selected objects to current active layer. Syntax: -ChangeToCurrentLayer

contexts.default: Interactive selection mode. Prompts to select objects, then moves them to whatever layer is currently active. Can combine with selection filters like _SelLast or _SelAll for efficiency.

-ChangeToCurrentLayer.errors: Fails if current layer is locked/hidden, or selected objects are on locked layers. Hidden objects won't be selectable without special selection commands.

-CopyToLayer.quick: -CopyToLayer [objects] [layer] | Creates duplicates on target layer, originals stay put

contexts.organization: Duplicates geometry across layers for different design iterations or backup copies while preserving originals
contexts.workflow: Use when you need the same objects on multiple layers - common for creating layer-based design alternatives
contexts.automation: Can create new layers automatically if they don't exist, making it useful for scripted workflows

-CopyToLayer.errors: Dash prefix means no dialog - typos in layer names create unwanted layers; overlapping duplicates if run repeatedly

-OneLayerOn.quick: -OneLayerOn LayerName | Isolates one layer, hides all others

contexts.modeling: Quick isolation for working on specific geometry without visual clutter from other layers
contexts.drafting: Focus on single drawing layer while hiding construction lines, dimensions, or annotations
contexts.analysis: Isolate objects by layer for measurement, inspection, or modification without interference

-OneLayerOn.errors: Nonexistent layer names fail silently; all other layers hidden including important references

-OneLayerOff.quick: Hides one layer. Cannot turn off current active layer - switch first.

contexts.default: Prompts to select layer by name or picker. Use exact case-sensitive names when typing directly.

-OneLayerOff.errors: Fails silently on current layer. No effect if layer already hidden.

contexts.layer_management: Essential for isolating work to specific layers. Use with ShowSelected/HideSelected for layer-based workflows. Combine with SelNone first to ensure clean selection.
contexts.object_filtering: Part of selection toolkit alongside SelObjectType, SelVisible. Layer visibility affects results - ensure target layer is visible before selecting.
contexts.batch_operations: Select all layer objects before applying transformations, material changes, or deletions. Useful for layer cleanup and organization tasks.

-SelObjectsOnLayer.errors: Misspelled layer names result in no selection. Hidden/locked objects ignored. Layer must exist in document or command fails silently.

contexts.default: Select cutting objects first, then objects to trim. Negative prefix changes selection behavior from standard Trim.
contexts.cuttingobjects=no: _-Trim _CuttingObjects=No skips cutting object selection, goes directly to selecting objects to trim.
contexts.no_cutting_objects: Trim without boundaries - select objects to trim directly, useful for self-trimming operations.

-Trim.errors: Fails if expecting standard Trim behavior - negative prefix inverts selection sequence

-Fillet.quick: _-Fillet _Radius {value} | Must set radius BEFORE selecting edges

contexts.edge_filleting: Works on polysurface edges. Radius limited by smallest adjacent face dimension. Complex intersections may fail with large radii.
contexts.curve_filleting: Creates arc transitions between curves. Both curves must be in same plane. Radius affects how much of original curves gets trimmed.
contexts.surface_filleting: Creates blend surfaces between surfaces. More complex than edge fillets. Consider Join=Yes to merge results automatically.

-Fillet.errors: Fails if radius > smallest geometry dimension. Complex intersections fail with large radii. No radius set = no operation.

-Chamfer.quick: Sets chamfer parameters first, then prompts for edge selection. Distances measured along surfaces, not chamfer width.

contexts.distances: Use _Distances for asymmetric chamfers with different values on each side of edge. First distance applies to first selected surface.
contexts.uniform: Default mode applies same distance to both sides. Use _Distance option to explicitly set uniform value.
contexts.angle: Use _Angle option to define chamfer by one distance and angle instead of two distances for more intuitive control.

-Chamfer.errors: Fails when distances exceed available surface area or are too small/large relative to edge length.
